response.title: solar setup for a small boat with no shore power to keep a fridge running
response.answer:
For a small boat with no shore power, I'd recommend a 12V solar system with a LiFePO4 battery to keep the refrigerator running 24/7, including overnight.

The key is to size the system for cloudy days, not just sunny afternoons.

Recommended solar setup

Assuming you have a small, efficient 12V marine compressor refrigerator (rather than a household refrigerator):

RECOMMENDED STARTING CONFIGURATION

Solar panels

300–400W

Battery

200Ah
12V LiFePO4

Charge controller

30–40A MPPT

Fridge power

12V DC

This is a good starting point for an efficient compressor fridge using roughly 400–600Wh per day, with reasonable sun exposure. Actual sizing depends on your location, season, and fridge consumption.

How the system connects

Solar panels

300–400W

MPPT solar charge controller

30–40A, properly rated for panel voltage

12V 200Ah LiFePO4 battery

Approximately 2.56kWh nominal storage

12V marine refrigerator

Powered through a fused DC circuit

You would also need marine-rated wiring, appropriate fuses or breakers, battery disconnects, and secure, corrosion-resistant mounting. A dedicated house battery should be isolated from the engine-starting battery.

Avoid using a 120V inverter if the refrigerator can run directly on 12V DC. That saves energy.

Example components

Renogy 16BB N-Type 200W 24V Monocrystalline Solar Panel for …

Two panels for 400W total

$179.00 each

Redodo 12V 200Ah PLUS Lithium LiFePO4 Battery Max 2560W Powe…

200Ah battery; verify marine suitability and BMS specifications

$449.99

VICTRON ENERGY SmartSolar MPPT 100/30, SCC110030210

30A MPPT controller for the proposed array, subject to panel electrical specifications

$139.99

How much solar is actually necessary?

For a fridge consuming 500Wh/day, here's an illustrative comparison assuming four peak sun-hours and 75% overall solar output efficiency.

Boat shading, cloudy weather and winter conditions can substantially reduce these numbers.

1. What type of refrigerator?

Regular 120V household fridge

2. How big is your boat?
Under 20 feet

Over 30 feet
3. How long must the fridge run?
Weekends / occasional trips
24/7, even when nobody is aboard
Full-time during boating season
Size my solar system

The biggest distinction is whether you want the refrigerator to stay running unattended for weeks or only while you're using the boat. For unattended operation, I'd build in substantially more margin for extended cloudy weather and provide battery monitoring and a low-voltage alert. Solar alone cannot guarantee uninterrupted refrigeration through arbitrarily long periods without sunlight.

The key is to size the system for cloudy days, not just sunny afternoons.

## Recommended solar setup

Assuming you have a small, efficient 12V marine compressor refrigerator (rather than a household refrigerator):

  <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">RECOMMENDED STARTING CONFIGURATION</text>
  <grid columns={2} gap={3}>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Solar panels</text>
      <title size="xl" color="default">300–400W</title>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Battery</text>
      <title size="xl" color="default">200Ah</title>
      <caption>12V LiFePO4</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Charge controller</text>
      **30–40A MPPT**
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Fridge power</text>
      **12V DC**
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <text color="secondary" size="sm">This is a good starting point for an efficient compressor fridge using roughly 400–600Wh per day, with reasonable sun exposure. Actual sizing depends on your location, season, and fridge consumption.</text>
</box>

## How the system connects

<box border radius="lg" padding={3} gap={2} align="center">
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="md" padding={3} width="80%" align="center" gap={1}>
    <icon name="sun" color="secondary" size="lg"/>
    **Solar panels**
    <caption>300–400W</caption>
  </box>
  <icon name="arrow-down" color="tertiary" size="lg"/>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="md" padding={3} width="80%" align="center" gap={1}>
    <icon name="sliders-horizontal" size="lg"/>
    **MPPT solar charge controller**
    <caption>30–40A, properly rated for panel voltage</caption>
  </box>
  <icon name="arrow-down" color="tertiary" size="lg"/>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="md" padding={3} width="80%" align="center" gap={1}>
    <icon name="battery-charging" size="lg"/>
    **12V 200Ah LiFePO4 battery**
    <caption>Approximately 2.56kWh nominal storage</caption>
  </box>
  <icon name="arrow-down" color="tertiary" size="lg"/>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="md" padding={3} width="80%" align="center" gap={1}>
    <icon name="refrigerator" size="lg"/>
    **12V marine refrigerator**
    <caption>Powered through a fused DC circuit</caption>
  </box>
</box>

You would also need marine-rated wiring, appropriate fuses or breakers, battery disconnects, and secure, corrosion-resistant mounting. A dedicated house battery should be isolated from the engine-starting battery.

Avoid using a 120V inverter if the refrigerator can run directly on 12V DC. That saves energy.

## Example components

  <row align="start" gap={3}>

    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>

    <box flex="1" gap={1}>

    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## How much solar is actually necessary?

For a fridge consuming 500Wh/day, here's an illustrative comparison assuming four peak sun-hours and 75% overall solar output efficiency.

| Solar capacity | Daily production | Assessment |
|---|---:|---|
| 100W | 300Wh | Insufficient |
| 200W | 600Wh | Marginal |
| 300W | 900Wh | Good |
| 400W | 1,200Wh | More margin |

Boat shading, cloudy weather and winter conditions can substantially reduce these numbers. <Cite refs={["turn634746search2","turn634746search4"]}/>

## Three questions to size it correctly

{@body const [fridge,setFridge] = DIL.useState("12v")}
{@body const [boat,setBoat] = DIL.useState("small")}
{@body const [duration,setDuration] = DIL.useState("continuous")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Size a boat solar refrigeration system for me. Fridge: "+fridge+". Boat: "+boat+". Usage: "+duration+". Recommend exact panel wattage, battery Ah, and charging equipment.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>1. What type of refrigerator?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={fridge} onChange={setFridge}>
        <radio value="12v">12V compressor fridge</radio>
        <radio value="120v">Regular 120V household fridge</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Not sure / haven't bought one</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>2. How big is your boat?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={boat} onChange={setBoat}>
        <radio value="small">Under 20 feet</radio>
        <radio value="medium">20–30 feet</radio>
        <radio value="large">Over 30 feet</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>3. How long must the fridge run?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={duration} onChange={setDuration}>
        <radio value="weekends">Weekends / occasional trips</radio>
        <radio value="continuous">24/7, even when nobody is aboard</radio>
        <radio value="seasonal">Full-time during boating season</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Size my solar system <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

The biggest distinction is whether you want the refrigerator to **stay running unattended for weeks** or only while you're using the boat. For unattended operation, I'd build in substantially more margin for extended cloudy weather and provide battery monitoring and a low-voltage alert. Solar alone cannot guarantee uninterrupted refrigeration through arbitrarily long periods without sunlight.
